reason: The MVP acceptance walk recurs at each MVP close. Its verdict rules (what counts as a pass, how agent gaps and orchestrator-run steps are recorded, how gate counts are sourced, what stays NOT RUN) were improvised in one session. No existing skill covers the end-of-MVP checklist verdict, so create it as a class-level verification skill.
Ivan's 2026-11-02 MVP goal set a hard no-silence rule and a document-don't-pretend rule for deferred items. Neither is in the walk skill, so findings were triaged without it.

The episode held copy fixes until the backtest reported, because editing would break its exact-string checks. That ordering is a repeatable rule for any acceptance walk, and it is not yet written down.

The brief paraphrased a recipe from memory and named the wrong mail-catcher API. The correct recipe already lives in eventar-live-verify-worktree. A walk-level rule to copy recipes from the skill prevents the same drift on the next dispatch.

Browser lenses were dispatched without a pane-wake step. They got empty read_page results from a hidden Browser pane, then fell back to synthetic DOM events, so their dead-control findings could not be proven. The wake sequence belongs in every browser-lens brief, and synthetic events must not stand in for clicks.

This walk's useful procedures were not in the acceptance-walk skill: the three-state time-gate walk, the re-click before keeping a no-response finding, and the walk-in identity read-back. The helper was left only in the session scratchpad, which a future walk cannot reach.

Orchestrator confirmed by SQL that a closed check-in window was enforced on the attendee desk but not on the speaker write path, a silent data write. The existing time-gated bullet covers one desk; this adds enumerating every writer to the table so the next walk tests them all.

Browser lenses repeatedly spent their 40-call caps on pane wakes and a slow venue picker before reaching window-critical steps. The orchestrator took steps 6-8 over itself with batches and got clean by-execution passes. The skill says to mark such steps but not when to take them over.

Run 2 of the MVP walk found the practitioner wizard asks users to accept Terms and Privacy documents that do not exist. The walk skill has no row for copy that points at a missing page, so the next walk could pass it as copy-only.

Re-walk of MVP fixes on 2026-11-06 wrote a publish PASS from the event creator's own run and noted it did not test the non-creator path. The walk skill has no rule that makes the actor relation explicit, so a creator-only pass can read as a full pass.

Organiser walk on 2026-11-14 reported S7 NOT RUN because the analytics CSV is the funnel summary, not the registrants export; its window-shift helper also failed on events with agenda blocks after the S5 trigger landed. Both are procedure gaps in the walk skill.
Walk row verdicts were drawn from the wrong entry path. A landing check that enters via a deep link does not prove the cold-start landing. The row must name its entry path.
The practitioner lens built a race test out of SQL fill plus a click, which is a reusable technique. The walk skill has no recipe for it, so the next walk would reinvent it or skip the race.

A disabled control with no visible reason is a known rule, but the walk skill never tells the walker to test wrong-turn inputs for it. The practitioner lens found one this way and left three wrong turns unrun.

At wrap-up the orchestrator had to re-verify a review-separation claim from memory and soften an unverified count from truncated git output; the walk skill has no rule for verifying the summary's own provenance claims.
The MVP walk ran inline on the main model, used up its allowance, and stopped twice before the report. The walk skill has no rule for splitting persona walks into dispatches.
Pause handoff left the walk report and a large sweep outside the repo; the next agent had no durable copy. Adds a concrete pause checklist to the walk skill.

Episode resumed the MVP walk and frontend coherence pass. The agent counted 46 uncommitted product files, found a red check:ui-primitives gate, and stopped. It guessed that the gate hits predated the diff without running the HEAD check. It also filtered .claude/skills deletions out of git status with grep -v without reporting them. The walk skill has no preflight for an unnamed uncommitted tree or for baseline attribution before the walk starts, so the next run would repeat this stop or walk on a caveated tree.

The walk skill names the cookie-jar clash only indirectly through the shared-fixture rule in subagent-dispatch. Persona walks on this run were sequenced by the orchestrator for this reason, and the rule belongs in the walk skill where briefs are written.

The r4 practitioner hand-back re-reported findings that were already open in r3 and, for the consent dead end, since 2026-11-03, as MINOR/NIT/known items. The walk skill has rules for finding quality and consent copy but none that escalates a carried-forward finding to Ivan as a ruling. Adding that rule closes the gap without duplicating existing dispatch or live-verify guidance, which already cover the other incidents in this window.

On r4 the orchestrator closed the walk with a wrap_up asking Ivan to choose the M1 consent wording ("Wait for legal" / "Reword now") with no render of either option. The standing 2026-11-21 rule requires before and after frames before any frontend decision question. This walk bullet is what told the orchestrator to ask in prose, so it must name the frame requirement.

The r4 walk reported "every gate is green except 4 old primitives hits" and its verdict named only the open MAJOR as the reason done stayed open. The check:ui-primitives gate was red, and the skill says one red gate keeps done open. Wording that softens a red gate to "green except" hides the reason from the reader. The rule needs to say a pre-existing red gate still counts in the verdict.
